description: Static evaluation set for the demo. The corpus is three clusters of three same-brand models plus three short manuals. Each symptom query is answered by exactly one model's troubleshooting section (the `entry`, written into that manual at generation time and absent from its siblings). `unique_terms` must appear only in the target manual; check with `uv run python src/chunk_rescorer/check_queries.py`. Spec queries are answered near the front of a manual, where the reranker sees the text with or without chunk_rescorer.

symptom_queries.query: pressure washer water flow drops off after a few minutes, inlet filter screen collapsed
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: Water flow at the nozzle drops off after a few minutes of spraying, and the garden hose inlet filter screen (part RP-IS-26) is found collapsed inward when the supply hose is removed.
Possible cause: The RP-IS-26 filter screen was installed with its dome facing inward, so supply pressure folds it into the inlet passage and chokes flow as the pump warms.
Corrective action: Shut off the engine and water supply, unscrew the garden hose from the pump inlet, remove the RP-IS-26 screen, reshape or replace it, and reinstall it with the dome facing outward toward the hose before reconnecting.

symptom_queries.query: pressure washer pump drips from weep hole when trigger released
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: Water drips steadily from the weep hole on the underside of the pump whenever the spray gun trigger is released, although spraying pressure is normal.
Possible cause: The pump's low-pressure seals (seal kit RP-LS-32) are worn; the weep hole is designed to vent water that passes a worn seal so it does not reach the crankcase.
Corrective action: Stop the engine, relieve pressure by squeezing the trigger, remove the four pump manifold bolts, replace the low-pressure seals with kit RP-LS-32, apply the supplied silicone grease to the plungers, reassemble, and confirm the weep hole stays dry.

symptom_queries.query: pressure washer pump oil looks milky in the sight glass
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: The oil in the triplex pump's sight glass has turned milky or cloudy white, and the pump runs noticeably louder.
Possible cause: Water has passed the plunger seals into the pump crankcase and emulsified with the pump oil; the milky appearance in the sight glass is the first sign of seal wear on the triplex pump.
Corrective action: Stop the engine, drain the pump crankcase through the drain plug, replace the plunger seals, refill with 12 ounces of Ridgeline RP-PO-40 pump oil to the center of the sight glass, and check the sight glass again after one hour of use.

symptom_queries.query: garage door opener chain sagging and slapping the rail, door jerks at the top
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: The drive chain sags below the rail, slaps against it during travel, and the door jerks as it reaches the top of its travel.
Possible cause: The chain has stretched with use and the chain tension bolt (part KC-TB-8) at the trolley has not been readjusted; a chain that hangs more than a quarter inch below the rail will skip on the sprocket.
Corrective action: Disconnect power, tighten the KC-TB-8 chain tension bolt with a 7/16-inch wrench until the chain rides a quarter inch above the base of the rail, cycle the door twice, and recheck the sag.

symptom_queries.query: garage door only opens halfway and opener light flashes 3-1 pattern
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: The garage door opens about halfway, stops, and the motor unit light flashes in a 3-1 pattern (three flashes, pause, one flash).
Possible cause: The up-travel limit was reset to its factory midpoint when the unit switched to backup battery power and back (diagnostic 3-1, travel limits unlearned).
Corrective action: Press and hold the Program and Up buttons on the motor unit together until the light blinks twice, press Up until the door is fully open, press Program once to store the up limit, then run one complete open-close cycle and confirm the 3-1 pattern has stopped.

symptom_queries.query: garage door opener camera shows a black image at night and the light won't turn on
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: The integrated camera shows a black image at night while the daytime picture is normal, and the motion-activated light does not turn on when someone enters the garage.
Possible cause: The camera's privacy shutter (slide KC-PS-15) was left closed after installation; with the shutter closed the infrared night-vision emitters and the motion sensor behind it are blocked.
Corrective action: Slide the KC-PS-15 privacy shutter fully open on the front of the motor unit, then in the Kestrel app open Camera Settings and turn Night Vision back on; confirm the motion light responds by walking beneath the unit.

symptom_queries.query: generator fuel valve only turns halfway and engine starves under load
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: The fuel shutoff valve lever (part RG-FV-45) turns only to a halfway detent, and the engine starts but starves and stalls as soon as a load is connected.
Possible cause: The shipping detent pin under the RG-FV-45 lever, fitted to keep the valve closed in transit, has not been removed, so the valve cannot rotate to the fully open position.
Corrective action: Stop the engine, pull the red shipping detent pin straight out from beneath the fuel shutoff valve lever, rotate the lever fully to ON, and restart the engine under load.

symptom_queries.query: generator twist-lock outlet dead but GFCI duplex outlets work
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: The engine runs normally and all four 120V GFCI duplex outlets work, but the 120/240V twist-lock outlet is dead.
Possible cause: The twist-lock outlet is protected by its own 30-amp thermal breaker (part RG-TB-30) behind the outlet panel, separate from the main circuit breaker, and it has tripped after a sustained overload on that outlet alone.
Corrective action: Stop the engine, remove the two outlet panel screws, press the reset stud on the RG-TB-30 thermal breaker until it clicks, reduce the load on the twist-lock outlet below 30 amps, then restart and confirm output at the twist-lock outlet.

symptom_queries.query: dual fuel generator runs on gasoline but stalls within seconds after switching to propane
symptom_queries.entry:
Problem: The engine runs normally on gasoline but stalls within a few seconds after the fuel selector is moved to PROPANE, even with a full propane tank connected.
Possible cause: The propane regulator's excess-flow safety (part RG-PR-10) has tripped because the tank valve was opened quickly, and it now restricts propane flow to a trickle.
Corrective action: Move the fuel selector to OFF, close the propane tank valve, wait thirty seconds for the RG-PR-10 excess-flow safety to reset, reopen the tank valve slowly no more than a quarter turn at first, then set the selector to PROPANE and restart.
